what_worked: Slide 6 quality-of-book cut and slide 9 MoR-switcher wedge are genuinely original, decision-useful analyses.
fix_next: Reconcile the $133.8m headline with the $15.6M dataset total; disclose any filter or annualization method explicitly on the slide.
verdict: Strong framing and honesty about limits, but key revenue figures don't reconcile with the dataset.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: top-10 share 50.6% vs reference 49.6% (~1pp off). Slide 3: $133.8m 'verified 12-month card volume' does not reconcile with dataset total $15.6M even annualized ($187M); derivation unstated. Slide 5: Stripe volume share 90.9% vs reference 86.7% ($13.5M/$15.6M).

evidence.insight: Slide 6 compares % of accounts ≥$10k MRR across processors, surfacing that specialist platforms (Superwall, Whop) convert ~45% vs cohort 21%. Slide 9 identifies 14% MoR switchers carrying only 1.8% volume as a compliance-driven wedge. These are non-obvious, decision-relevant cuts.
evidence.narrative: Arc moves from data credibility (2) → market shape (3-6) → compliance thesis (7-9) → NRI corridor (10-12) → solution (13-14) → ask (15) → caveats (16). Coherent but the pivot from dataset analysis to NRI pitch (slides 10-13) is abrupt; the dataset barely informs the NRI corridor section, weakening the data-story thread.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 flags missingness (country 76%, category 73%), marks NRI figures as illustrative, distinguishes dataset from external sources. Slide 16 dedicates a full page to caveats. Audience (seed investors) and scope are clear. Exemplary epistemic hygiene.
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 share overstated by ~1pp (50.6 vs 49.6). $133.8m headline is unexplained — dataset total is $15.6M, annualized ≈$187M, not $133.8m; no filter or methodology disclosed. Stripe volume share 90.9% vs reference 86.7%. Country/category missingness percentages are correct. Median $3,069 on slide 4 is plausible but unverifiable against reference.
evidence.visual: Clean dark theme, consistent orange accent, legible tables. Only two actual data charts (slides 4, 6) across 16 slides — the rest is text and big-number callouts. Two section-divider slides (7, 10) carry zero information. Restrained but under-visualized for a data story.
evidence.ai_slop: None detected. Domain-specific regulatory knowledge (NRE/NRO, SEBI, FATCA/CRS, PIS/LRS) is authentic. No generic filler or inflated language.

change_reason: Lowered accuracy from 6.5→5.5: the $133.8m headline is the deck's anchor number and cannot be reconciled with the dataset; this is more serious than a rounding issue. Lowered narrative from 8→7.5: the transition from dataset analysis to NRI pitch is abrupt and the dataset barely supports the corridor thesis. Reduced bonus from 3→2: the deck is impressive as a pitch but the data-story component is thinner than the preliminary score implied — only ~6 of 16 slides engage the dataset substantively.
